passage_notes: Factual check: Passage A matches Madrian & Shea (2001): large US firm, auto-enrollment in 1998; participation ~37% under old rule vs ~86% for auto-enrolled hires (3-15 months tenure); largest effects among young and lower-income (also women, Black and Hispanic) workers. Default was 3% contribution into a money market fund, consistent with Passage B. Madrian & Shea also noted some participants anchored at the lower default rate. Accurate.
Passage B's escalation program matches Thaler & Benartzi's Save More Tomorrow (2004): savings rates rose from ~3.5% to ~13.6% over ~40 months (nearly quadrupled), so 'more than tripled' is accurate.
minor: In Passage A the company's matching contribution existed under both rules; fine. 'late 1990s' fine.
